1. Acceptance of Terms

By downloading, installing, or using Mint (“the Software”), you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service (“Terms”). If you do not agree to these Terms, do not use the Software. We reserve the right to update these Terms at any time, and your continued use of the Software constitutes acceptance of any changes.

Continuing from Welcome indicates that you agree to these Terms and acknowledge the Privacy Policy. From Direct 1.0.76 and Setapp 1.0.36, usage sharing is on by default after you acknowledge the disclosure on Welcome. A choice you made earlier is kept; installations that acknowledged the earlier policy without choosing are asked once before this default applies. You can turn usage sharing off under Account > Share my usage statistics without losing functionality. The limited app-opened and setup signals described in the Privacy Policy continue when sharing is off. Earlier Direct and Setapp versions required a separate choice to enable usage analytics. The Mac App Store edition requires your separate analytics choice before collecting any Mint product event, including setup completion; accepting these Terms alone does not authorize that collection. You can decline optional analytics or turn them off in Settings without losing product functionality.

2. Description of Service

Mint is a macOS desktop application that helps users organize, categorize, and manage files on their local computer. The Software uses on-device technologies including OCR (via Apple Vision), metadata analysis, language detection, and image classification to analyze and organize files. All processing occurs locally on your Mac.

3. Access Tiers
Current Direct Free Tier

The Direct Free tier is free to download and to keep using, without an account or payment information. Disk scans and memory release, whether manual or through Auto Care, are free without time or usage limits. From Direct 1.0.96, cleaning and organizing share one free allowance of 1 GB a week, resetting on Monday. Cleanup counts bytes removed or rewritten by Disk cleanup, storage optimization (Optimize), compression, app uninstall and removal of app leftovers, Trash removal, and package-manager cleanup, including cleanup through the Direct CLI or MCP. Organizing counts the size of the files Mint successfully moves. A run skips files that do not fit the remaining allowance and can continue with smaller files; skipped files stay in place. Manual use and Auto Care share this allowance. Onboarding is provided free of charge: actions taken during the first-run setup do not consume the weekly allowance. After setup, the first cleanup and every later cleanup or organizing run count toward the same allowance. Failed moves consume nothing; undo does not refund usage. Cleaning or organizing beyond the remaining weekly allowance requires paid access or the next reset. Package-manager cleanup requires its whole checked scope to fit because the operation cannot be split. Auto Care for Disk, memory, and folders is included in the Direct Free tier from Direct 1.0.92, without a plan or trial. When the shared allowance is spent, Disk and folder Auto Care pause until the reset; memory Auto Care continues. Using the free tier never starts an automatic charge. Feature availability is listed on the pricing and edition comparison. Earlier releases retain the access model described in section 4.

Paid Access

Mint Unlimited removes the shared weekly allowance for cleanup, organizing and Auto Care, within the features supported by your edition and installed version. Auto Care operates while Mint is running, after you enable it, within the supported categories, folders, permissions, schedules, and memory settings you choose. When paid access ends, the Direct Free tier described above applies again, and Disk scans and memory release remain free. The Direct free allowances and these feature boundaries do not replace the separate Mac App Store or Setapp terms.

Current Direct website customers may choose a One-Time license for 1–5 Macs they own or use: $39.99 for the first Mac and $20 for each additional Mac ($59.99, $79.99, $99.99 or $119.99 for 2, 3, 4 or 5 Macs). Rent to Own covers one Mac at $9.99 per month for four monthly payments ($39.96 total before applicable tax). Rent to Own provides Unlimited access from the first payment and ends its scheduled charges after the fourth payment, when ownership is retained. A One-Time purchase includes every Mint 1.x release, and installed versions may be used indefinitely. Rent to Own ownership includes the same. This applies to purchases made before October 9, 2026 as well. A later major version, if one is released, may be offered as a separate, optional purchase, and it does not disable any version you already have. The Mac App Store offers its own Monthly subscription and one-time Lifetime purchase, with marketplace-specific trial and access terms. Setapp access follows the plan and terms shown by Setapp. Direct purchases do not replace marketplace purchases.

Invites and Banked Cleanup

Direct Mint users signed in with a verified email address may invite others. When a friend claims an invite on a Mac new to Mint, the friend receives 20 GB of banked cleanup. A Mac is new to Mint for 48 hours after Mint first opens on it, so the friend has 48 hours to claim. After the friend’s cleaning or organizing in Mint frees at least 1 GB, the inviter receives 20 GB. Only cleaning and organizing done after the claim count toward that 1 GB, and nothing done during Mint’s first-run setup counts. An inviter receives this for at most 10 invites per calendar year (UTC). Each Mac, each account, and each email address can claim one invite. An invite cannot be claimed on a virtual machine, on the inviter’s own Macs, by the inviter’s other accounts, with a throwaway email address, or from the network of a large cloud hosting provider. One network can claim at most 5 invites a day, and an inviter can have at most 3 friends whose email addresses share a domain, unless it is a large email provider’s. The inviter receives nothing for a friend who has used one of the inviter’s Macs, or whose Mac the inviter has used. Banked cleanup belongs to the Mint account that received it. It is one balance, used on any Mac where the Direct edition of Mint is signed in to that account. The free weekly allowance is 1 GB a week on each Mac. On each Mac, banked cleanup is used for cleaning and organizing only after that Mac’s weekly allowance is spent, and only while no paid access is active on that Mac. It does not reset and does not expire. Banked cleanup cannot be given or moved to another account. A gift link created before October 17, 2026 can still be claimed once, and not with a throwaway email address. Banked cleanup has no cash value. It cannot be exchanged for money or paid access, and it cannot be sold, bought, or transferred for money or anything of value. We may withhold, remove, or reverse banked cleanup obtained through fake accounts, automated means, or other abuse of these Terms. We may change or end the invite program for new invites; ending it does not remove banked cleanup already in an account.

4. Earlier Releases and Existing Purchases

Direct 1.0.92 through 1.0.95 have separate weekly allowances of 1 GB cleanup and 50 organized files. Direct 1.0.92 through 1.0.96 also included a free first manual cleanup after setup, in addition to the setup gift. Earlier Direct releases distributed as Mint Free had a weekly allowance of up to 210 organized files and 3.5 GB cleaned, resetting every Monday. Direct 1.0.36 offered a seven-day full-feature trial, after which scanning remained available and other actions required paid access. Direct releases between 1.0.36 and 1.0.92 had a shared 1 GB cleanup allowance that never reset, and from Direct 1.0.83 they included one seven-day Auto Care trial per Mac that ended by itself. Access terms depend on the installed version; the current download uses the free tier described in section 3. Existing purchases retain the entitlement on the order receipt; this clarification does not revoke them. Customers can sign in with their verified purchase email to restore paid access or manage the connected Mac.

5. Payment and Refunds

Direct website purchases are processed securely through Lemon Squeezy. Existing recurring subscriptions, including Annual plans, follow their order terms. Current Rent to Own charges monthly for four payments and then stops; it is not an indefinite subscription. You may cancel through Lemon Squeezy’s order portal before the next billing date; cancellation takes effect at the end of the current paid period. If Rent to Own is canceled before completion, access follows the installed version’s unpaid terms after the paid period, and payment progress is retained. Resume through the order portal, or contact support before starting a replacement plan so your progress can be carried forward. Completed ownership is not canceled by the end of scheduled payments. Prices, billing periods, renewal terms, and applicable taxes are displayed before purchase. Mac App Store purchases are processed by Apple through In-App Purchase. Setapp Marketplace purchases are processed by Setapp, which manages licensing, payments, applicable taxes, and first-line billing and licensing support for the Setapp edition.

Direct purchase refunds: We want you to be satisfied with Mint. If you are not happy with a direct website charge, you may request a full refund within 30 days of that charge. To request a refund, contact us through our website or reply to your purchase confirmation email. Refunds are processed through Lemon Squeezy and typically appear within 5–10 business days. This policy does not limit any non-waivable consumer rights that apply to you.

App Store purchase refunds: Refunds for App Store purchases are handled by Apple under Apple Media Services terms. To request a refund for an App Store purchase, use Apple’s purchase history and refund flow.

Setapp purchase refunds and cancellations: Refunds, cancellations, renewals, and billing support for purchases made through the Setapp Marketplace are handled by Setapp under the terms and purchase flow presented by Setapp.

While we strive to make Mint reliable and accurate, no software can guarantee perfect file organization in every scenario. We recommend reviewing Mint’s proposed changes before applying them and maintaining regular backups of your important files.

7. User Responsibility for Files

You are solely responsible for your files and data. Mint provides tools to organize and manage your files, including an undo feature that allows you to reverse recent file operations. However:

We do not guarantee that all operations can be undone in every circumstance.
We are not responsible for any data loss, file corruption, or unintended file modifications that may occur during use of the Software.
We strongly recommend maintaining independent backups of your files before using any automated file organization tool, including Mint.
The undo history is stored locally and may be cleared if you uninstall the application or delete its support files.

IN NO EVENT SHALL WE BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF PROFITS, OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO YOUR USE OF THE SOFTWARE.

9. Account and Access Restrictions

Direct paid access is tied to the verified Mint account that claims the purchase and may be connected to the number of Macs stated at checkout and on the receipt (one Mac if no other allowance is stated). We reserve the right to suspend accounts or entitlements that are shared, redistributed, obtained fraudulently, or used in violation of these Terms. App Store entitlements are tied to the Apple Account used for purchase and are managed through Apple. Setapp entitlements and device limits are tied to the applicable Setapp account and purchase and are managed through Setapp. If you believe access was suspended or unavailable in error, please contact the support channel for the distribution platform where you obtained Mint.

10. Updates and Support

Updates are provided through the distribution channel where you obtained the Software, including direct downloads from our website, Sparkle updates, Mac App Store updates, or Setapp updates. An active direct subscription includes access to current releases. A direct One-Time purchase, and Rent to Own once owned, includes every Mint 1.x release; a later major version may be offered separately and is optional, and it does not disable any version you already have. We will make reasonable efforts to provide product support through our website contact form but do not guarantee specific response times or resolution of all issues. Setapp provides first-line support for Setapp billing and licensing matters.

11. Termination

You may stop using the Software at any time by uninstalling it from your Mac. You may cancel a direct subscription as described in Section 5; Unlimited remains available through the paid period, and afterward the installed version's free access applies. We may terminate or suspend paid access if you violate these Terms, in which case your right to Unlimited throughput may cease immediately. Sections of these Terms that by their nature should survive termination (including Intellectual Property, Limitation of Liability, and Disclaimer of Warranties) will remain in effect.

12. Limitation of Liability

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, OUR TOTAL LIABILITY TO YOU FOR ALL CLAIMS ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THESE TERMS OR THE SOFTWARE SHALL NOT EXCEED THE AMOUNT YOU PAID FOR YOUR MINT LICENSE IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

These Terms shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Mint team operates, without regard to conflict of law principles. Any disputes arising from these Terms or your use of the Software shall be resolved through good-faith negotiation, and if necessary, binding arbitration.

14. Changes to These Terms

We reserve the right to modify these Terms at any time. Updated Terms will be posted on this page with a revised “Last updated” date. Your continued use of the Software after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the updated Terms. For material changes, we will make reasonable efforts to notify users through the application or website.

You can turn usage sharing off under Account > Share my usage statistics. The disclosed app-opened and setup signals continue when sharing is off. Earlier Setapp versions required a separate choice to enable usage analytics. These records are not joined to Setapp customer or purchase data. Mint does not send Setapp your file contents, filenames, folder structure, or Mint activity and undo history. See our Privacy Policy and Setapp’s Privacy Notice for details.
